comment: Design-space synovial/extracellular KPV concentrations per route. The model uses C_ext as the boundary concentration for A1. IA is arithmetic from assumed dose and synovial volume; SC and oral are named PK assumptions because KPV systemic and synovial PK are poorly characterized. None is an efficacy or clinically achievable-exposure claim.

intra_articular.derivation: ARITHMETIC FROM NAMED DESIGN ASSUMPTIONS, not a clinical exposure claim. Central: assumed 0.2 mg KPV / 342.43 g/mol = 0.584 umol in an assumed 2 mL synovial compartment = 292 uM. Range crosses assumed 0.1-1 mg doses with assumed 2-20 mL compartments: 1 mg/2 mL = 1460 uM and 0.1 mg/20 mL = 15 uM after rounding. The dose and volume anchors are not source-qualified here. All values exceed the 10 nM cell-assay effective-concentration proxy, but their relation to the 160-1000 uM Km band varies.

subcutaneous.derivation: NAMED PK ASSUMPTION. 0.5 mg SC, bioavailability >80% (kpv-peptide.md). Peak plasma ~= dose/Vd with Vd ~ extracellular fluid (~15 L for a hydrophilic peptide): 0.5 mg/15 L = 33 ng/mL = ~0.10 uM peak plasma. Synovial fluid is a plasma ultrafiltrate; small-peptide synovial:plasma partition ~0.3-0.5 -> ~0.03-0.05 uM synovial peak. KPV plasma half-life is short (peptide, rapid clearance) so time-averaged synovial level is lower; central 0.030 uM (30 nM). Range 3-200 nM. The central value is ~3x the 10 nM extracellular cell-assay effective-concentration proxy; this is a thin engineering margin, not an efficacy prediction.

oral.derivation: NAMED PK ASSUMPTION. Oral KPV is primarily framed for local gut exposure; systemic and synovial delivery are poorly characterized. This design case assumes systemic exposure 10-100x below the SC design case, giving synovial KPV of 0.1-3 nM and a central 1 nM value (0.1x the extracellular cell-assay effective-concentration proxy). It is included only as a low-systemic-exposure case.
